summary.intent: Run the full GSD plan-phase → execute-phase pipeline for CipherBox phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings), producing research, validation, pattern-mapping, plans, and verified/executed waves, while also spinning up an independent worktree to prep phase 69 in parallel.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 was fully planned (12 plans/7 waves, research + Nyquist VALIDATION.md + pattern map, plan-checker PASSED, coverage gates 13/13) and execution proceeded sequentially through Wave 5 (9/12 plans done, plan 10 dispatched) with each wave independently spot-checked; a phase-69 worktree was created off origin/main for parallel independent work, not yet started.

repo: gsd-tools query commit reports `commit_failed` even when the commit actually lands in git log — a known false-negative; always verify with `git log` before treating it as a real failure.
worktree.baseRef must be 'head' (not the 'fresh'/origin-main default) for execute-phase worktrees, otherwise executors fork before the PLAN.md files exist on HEAD.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel execution is expensive (each worktree needs its own `pnpm install`) — sequential execution on the main tree is preferable when most waves are single-plan.
Web packages depend on a freshly rebuilt SDK dist; typecheck against a stale SDK dist is a recurring cross-package staleness landmine during phase 68.2 execution.

Executors tend to prematurely mark REQUIREMENTS.md checkboxes ([x]) for requirements whose acceptance criteria include a later deletion step (e.g. SDK-READ-01/02/03) — must be reverted to [ ] until the actual deletion plan lands.

Plan 11 (deleting ipns.service.ts, file-metadata.service.ts, kind-cache.ts, useFileSize.ts) has a much wider importer surface than originally scoped by the planner — utils/fileTypes.ts, lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts, vault-settings.store.ts, TextEditorDialog.tsx, useStreamingPreview.ts, and several components are unowned by any plan and will block deletion unless migrated first.

`resolveChildren` in packages/sdk/src/folder-listing.ts intentionally skips unresolvable/unsealable siblings (availability tradeoff) rather than swallowing the folder-level ROT-07 gate, since the target folder is already gated upstream via ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder.
The GSD post-planning gap-analysis check's JSON parser chokes on control characters in the `rendered` field — run the underlying check directly instead of parsing the wrapped output.
Intel API-surface extraction (§7.9) returned 0 symbols for this monorepo — it's HINT-only and safe to omit from planner prompts when empty.

code.finding: ROT-07 enforceResolved gate added to the root resolve path (resolvePublishedNode) in plan 68.2-01.
ROT-07 enforceResolved gate added to dfsFindFolder's child loop in plan 68.2-01, alongside the pre-existing write-path gate at line 1156.

Docstring documents the security reasoning for resolveChildren's skip-on-failure behavior — the folder is already gated before this runs, so an unverifiable sibling is omitted rather than rendered with stale/attacker content.

workflow: Independently re-running an executor's acceptance tests (rather than trusting its self-reported PASS) caught a legitimate premature-completion tracking bug (SDK-READ-01/02 marked done before deletion) that the executor's own summary didn't flag.

When computing a ScheduleWakeup delay across a session/quota interruption, recompute delaySeconds from a freshly-fetched current time immediately before the call — reusing an earlier timestamp produced a wake scheduled ~25 minutes late.

A user-requested pause was honored by letting the in-flight executor finish atomically (not killing it mid-edit) before halting dispatch, since each plan commits atomically and resuming from a clean HEAD is safe.
AskUserQuestion was used at two genuine decision gates (research vs. skip-research, and D-07 scope boundary) rather than assuming defaults, since both materially changed downstream plan scope.

friction: git fetch failed from the sandboxed session (no network access to GitHub); had to rely on the last-known local origin/main ref, verified as current by cross-checking against the 68.2 branch's fork point.
gsd-tools commit helper repeatedly reported false-negative `commit_failed` despite commits landing cleanly, requiring manual git log verification each time.
First ScheduleWakeup call used a stale timestamp and would have resumed 25 minutes late (04:35 instead of 04:10); had to be caught and corrected by the user's follow-up question.
Could not cleanly retract the incorrect 04:11 ScheduleWakeup after the user said to skip the wake and keep going — left as a harmless no-op.
zsh grep glob syntax failed when mapping deletion-blocking importers, requiring a retry with corrected syntax.
Post-planning gap-analysis parser choked on control characters in the tool's `rendered` output field, requiring a direct re-run of the underlying check.

Executors on two separate plans (01, 02, and again 03/05) prematurely marked SDK-READ requirement checkboxes complete before their deletion-dependent acceptance criteria were actually met, requiring manual REQUIREMENTS.md correction.
open_items: Phase 69 (Rust/Desktop FUSE + WinFsp) worktree created at cipher-box-phase69 off origin/main but planning/execution not yet started — user was pointed to /gsd-discuss-phase 69 first due to an underspecified grant-root scope algorithm and an open FUSE delete-authority-model question.
